product.title: Dehen for Dant - N-1 Waxed Deck Jacket - Hardtack, Kodiak
product.body_html:
The Dehen for Dant N-1 Waxed Deck Jacket returns in Hardtack and Kodiak, our own take on a tan waxed canvas we fell for last year and barely got to enjoy before it was gone. Rather than chase it, we worked with Dehen to develop our own interpretation, and it came out truly incredible. The finish is monochromatic, with the waxed shell, the mouton and even the canvas zipper pulls all living in the same warm family of tans, which carries the N-1 past vintage reproduction into something sleek, refined and modern. Hardtack takes its name from the dense ship's biscuit sailors lived on for months at sea, a fitting nod for a Navy deck jacket, while Kodiak is a rich, bear-brown mouton with real sheen. They sound like they belong together and look it even more, as if they were meant to be paired all along and we just got there first. It's a Dant exclusive with a custom Dant x Dehen label, in a color pairing that lives outside Dehen's regular lineup and only here.

The N-1 is the warmest jacket we carry, hands down. The body and collar are fully lined in genuine mouton, so a tee underneath is usually all it takes on the most frigid days, and the shearling is soft enough for bare skin with no itchies or scratchies. The 10 oz waxed canvas shell marbles from highs to lows as it creases, the kind of color shift that separates a great waxed garment from a flat one, and it only deepens as it picks up your own wear. Cuffs are 100% worsted wool knit on Dehen's 1940s machines in Portland, and a #10 army green brass zipper hides behind the six-button placket. The Navy first sent the N-1 to sea in WWII to keep deck crews warm on the North Atlantic, and 80-some years later this one is still more than up for the job.

product.title: 13oz - Foxfibre® Green Weft Selvedge - True Guy
product.body_html:
Iron is the quiet trick behind this fabric. Green FoxFibre® comes off the plant already carrying color, and treating it with iron, a mineral mordant that natural dyers have leaned on for centuries, sets off a reaction with the pigment already sitting inside the fiber rather than laying new color over the top of it. What comes out the other side is a deeper, steadier green-grey, and because the color lives in the fiber instead of coating it, washing and wear push the tone further along rather than stripping it away. Naked & Famous runs that weft against indigo rope-dyed warp yarns in a 13oz Japanese selvedge, which sets up the long game: as the indigo gives way at the knees and the seat, the green-grey underneath comes forward. Green is the difficult one in the FoxFibre® family. Sally Fox began selectively breeding naturally pigmented cotton in the 1980s to take chemical dyeing out of the equation, and the green variety she developed grows shorter fibers at much lower yields than the brown, which makes it harder to spin consistently and keeps the supply thin. For this denim the cotton is grown in the United States and the yarn is spun in Osaka, putting American organic agriculture and Japanese weaving on the same loom. A 5oz natural vegetable-tanned leather patch sits at the waistband, ready to darken and take on its own patina alongside the denim, with tin hardware and a button fly closing things out.

product.title: ONI Denim 222 "Asphalt" 20oz Super Wide Straight Jeans
product.body_html:
Asphalt is the right name. Dark, coarse and flecked with white, the surface of this 20oz denim looks more like tarmac than cloth, and it is where Oishi-san takes the two things ONI is known for — slub and nep — as far as they go. The yarn is spun with extreme variation in thickness, so the weave comes out rugged and irregular, and it is peppered with white cotton neps, the knots of short fiber most mills remove, which break the dark indigo surface with pale flecks. Woven on a shuttle loom at ultra-low tension, with a dark indigo warp over a white weft, it is one of the most tactile denims ONI has produced, and it is made in very limited quantities.

At this weight the fabric starts stiff and stays that way for a while; the reward is fading with real depth, where the neps and slubs catch the wear first and the indigo breaks unevenly around them.

The 222 is the widest cut in ONI's lineup: a super wide straight with a high rise, a relaxed waist and seat, and a leg that runs in one clean line to the hem with no taper. It takes oversized styling while keeping classic proportions, and it works with boots, sneakers or sandals alike.

Construction is ONI's own: custom copper doughnut buttons and hardware, punched copper rivets with hidden rivets on the back pockets, heavy-duty bar tacks, raised belt loops, a peek-a-boo selvedge coin pocket, cotton-lined front pockets and a vegetable-tanned cowhide leather patch, with the red selvedge ID at the outseam. Unsanforized and one-washed, ready to wear from the box. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size — we recommend taking your usual size. The 222 is a super wide straight with a high rise and no taper, so it is meant to sit with room from the waist down. The denim is unsanforized but has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected. With regular wear, the waistband will stretch approximately 1 inch, allowing the fit to settle comfortably over time. We don't recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart to find your perfect size.

product.title: TCB New Cats Drive Jeans
product.body_html:
Cats Drive is a riding cut. The original — a vintage denim jacket-and-jeans set from a cowboy brand, late 1940s to 1950s — comes from the era when jeans served coal miners, farmers and every trade going, yet this one was drawn for a man in the saddle: a rise high enough to stay put, a leg close enough not to bunch against the stirrup, and nothing spare. After about three years, TCB brings the series back, and these are its jeans.

The revival revisits one element: the fabric. TCB kept the EMOT cotton blend of the first run — East Memphis, New Orleans and Texas — but not its yarn. The original was woven with a 5.7-count warp and a 6.7-count weft, engineered for the long, continuous fading lines of left-hand twill; watching that batch age, the brand wanted the streaks longer still. Both warp and weft now sit at a 6-count, and the slubs have been lengthened to build more variation into the surface, so the denim fades in elongated vertical streaks rather than short breaks.

The cut follows the riding logic on the chart: a high rise (12.4" at the front on a 32) that sits at the natural waist, a close thigh and a slim straight leg tapering to a 7.7" opening — proportions made for boots, and for a jacket that closes at the waist.

Same name, different jeans: not a reproduction of the last version, but the Cats Drive reworked through the lens of TCB today. Made in Kojima, Japan.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size for TCB: the tagged size closely matches the actual waist measurement. Compared to most global American brands, sizing is similar or slightly smaller, so you may take the same size or one size up. The cut has a high rise, a close thigh and a slim straight leg with a 7.7" leg opening. In this case the denim is sanforized, so shrinkage is minimal and the measurements will hold; the waistband will give slightly with wear. We don't recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting pair to ensure the right fit.

product.title: TCB 13.5oz Baggy 50’s Jeans
product.body_html:
TCB started with the 50's. Thirteen years ago they were the first jeans the brand made — its first answer to the question of what the best jeans are — and every pair since has been measured against them: wider or slimmer, heavier or lighter, this tinge of indigo or that. When TCB began shipping overseas it drew a Slim 50's for foreign customers, the way Japanese cars are converted to left-hand drive for export. The Baggy 50's comes from the opposite direction. Young staff at TCB had been customizing the 50's pattern and wearing it baggy, and Inoue-san decided it deserved a proper shape — the same instinct that once had mods shrinking jeans in the bath and skaters buying them oversized. One pattern, read by a new generation.

Fabric and sewing specifications are exactly those of the 50's. The denim is approx. 13.5oz, 100% Zimbabwe cotton, woven on a vintage loom rather than a computer-regulated one, so the yarn thickness and tension vary naturally across the cloth. It fades the vintage way: white dots appear first, then join into long vertical lines. What changes is the silhouette — a modern wide cut with plenty of room through the hips, thighs and hem, on a high-set rise (12.2" at the front on a 32), with a slight taper to a 8.9" opening.

The construction is TCB's reproduction work at its most detailed. The paper patch is sewn on by hand, and around the time the fades come good it begins to tear, showing the dark blue beneath. Hidden rivets on the back pockets are attached by the most durable of the many period methods. Sewing thread is 100% cotton in four colors and five yarn counts, with seam widths matched to the vintage piece TCB owns and the vintage machines set up accordingly — down to the pocket bags, which were roughly sewn on the originals and are roughly sewn here, with the durability kept. Designed and made in Kojima, Japan.

Fit Notes: This model runs small: the waist measures 1–1.3" under the tagged size, roughly 2" less than a typical American pair of the same number. Compared to most global American brands, we recommend sizing up one from your usual size; in the larger sizes (36–38) the gap widens, so you may need to go up two. The cut is a baggy straight with a high-set rise, wide through the hips and thighs and roomy to the hem; the denim will give slightly at the waist with wear. We don't recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting pair to ensure the right fit.

product.title: TCB New Cats Drive Jacket
product.body_html:
The Cats Drive returns after about three years, and the change is in the yarn. The design itself stays where it was: a vintage denim jacket from a cowboy brand, dating from the late 1940s to the 1950s — made in an era when jeans were still tools for miners, farmers and every kind of worker, yet this one was drawn with a specific job in mind: riding a horse. That purpose shows in the cut, close through the body and shaped at the waist so nothing bunches in the saddle.

The fabric is where TCB has done the work. The original run used EMOT cotton — a blend drawn from East Memphis, New Orleans and Texas — with a 5.7-count warp and 6.7-count weft, engineered to produce the long, continuous fading lines that left-hand twill is known for. Watching that first batch age, the brand wanted the streaks longer still. So both warp and weft have been moved to a 6-count yarn, and the slubs have been lengthened, physically building more variation into the surface so that the fades run in elongated vertical streaks rather than short breaks. Same cotton, same twill direction, a different result in five years' time.

The name may be familiar, but this is not a reproduction of the last version — it is the Cats Drive rethought through the lens of TCB today. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: TCB's sizing is vintage-true: a size 42 measures 42.5" in the chest, with a tapered waist and a fitted hem, so the jacket sits close to the body the way the original did. We recommend taking your usual Japanese size for the intended fit — a 42 corresponds roughly to an American M–L — or sizing up one if you prefer room to layer a sweater underneath. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting jacket to ensure the right fit.

product.title: TCB New 50´s Type II Denim Jacket
product.body_html:
The 50's Jacket is the model TCB is best known for, and the one it has studied most closely. It follows a 1950s vintage Type II that TCB owns, examined down to the yarn count of every seam, with the shape adjusted for today: a slimmer chest, a longer body and tighter arms — a modern fit, but not so tight that it stops being a work jacket.

The denim is approx. 13.5oz, 100% Zimbabwe cotton, woven on a vintage loom rather than a computer-regulated one, so the thread thickness and tension vary naturally across the cloth. It fades the vintage way: white dots first, then the dots join into long vertical lines. The paper patch is made by hand, and around the time the fades come good it begins to tear, showing the dark blue underneath.

The sewing is where the reproduction goes deepest. The double stitching on the front pockets is done on a vintage two-needle machine, which leaves a small triangle where the two lines meet; the pocket flap is sewn in the same pass as the pocket, so the stitching runs unbroken from one to the other. The bar tacks match the original in width, thickness and placement, and all sewing thread is 100% cotton. On sizes above 40, the body is pieced at the side, as it was on the vintage jackets.

This version updates the last: the collar is 0.5 cm smaller; the cuffs and waistband are wider, matching the vintage exactly; shoulders gain 1 cm and the chest 2 cm; the body is 1.5 cm shorter and the sleeves 1 cm shorter; and the armhole opens by 3 cm around — small moves that make the jacket easier to wear without changing what it is. Designed and made in Kojima, Japan.

Fit Notes: The 50's Jacket has TCB's modern, trimmer fit — a slimmer chest, longer body and tighter arms than the vintage original. A size 42 measures 105 cm (41.3") in the chest, so it fits close, nearer to an American M than an L. We recommend taking your usual Japanese size for the intended fit, or sizing up one if you prefer room to layer a sweater underneath. Note that sizes above 40 have a pieced side seam (T-back), as on the vintage original. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting jacket to ensure the right fit.

product.title: Pure Blue Japan 14oz XX-019 Relaxed Tapered Jeans
product.body_html:
Every brand has one fabric it is known for. For Pure Blue Japan it is the XX: the 14oz slub selvedge denim that has been the brand's signature since the early 2000s and the reason it built a following far beyond Okayama. The yarn is the point — Pure Blue Japan's own slub threads, spun with deliberate irregularities in thickness, then woven on vintage shuttle looms at ultra-low tension so the unevenness stays in the cloth. The surface comes out rough, slubby and hairy in a way conventional spinning cannot reproduce, and the weavers stand behind it completely.

The fabric is dyed with a pure indigo warp over a white weft, and it fades the way XX has always faded: as the denim is worn in, the slub catches the wear first and fading spots appear across the surface, building a high-contrast character that rewards patience and daily use. It comes unsanforized and one-washed, so the sizing is settled and no further shrinkage is expected.

The 019 is Pure Blue Japan's relaxed tapered: a mid-high rise (10.8" at the front on a 32), generous room through the seat and thigh, and a strong taper from the knee to a narrow 6.7" leg opening. It carries the comfort of a roomy top block and resolves it into a clean line at the ankle — a natural fit for boots or sneakers alike.

Details hold to the brand's standard: custom iron buttons on a button fly, hidden copper rivets on the back pockets, raised belt loops, heavy-duty bar tacks, long stitching and a chain-stitched hem. The front pockets are lined in durable cotton, the coin pocket shows a peek-a-boo selvedge edge, and the blue selvedge ID sits at the outseam. The indigofera leaf embroidery on the back pocket and a lambskin leather patch finish it. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: These jeans run a bit small compared to most global American brands: the waist measures at or just under the tagged size. We recommend going one size up from your usual size, or taking your usual size only if you want a snug fit from day one. The 019 is a relaxed tapered with a mid-high rise. The denim is unsanforized and one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected, and it stretches at the waist with wear (up to 1"). We don't recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting garment to ensure the right fit.

product.title: Pure Blue Japan DNP-019-IDSM 16oz Double Nep "Indigo x Sumi" Relaxed Tapered Jeans
product.body_html:
Most mills comb neps out of their yarn. Pure Blue Japan leaves them in, and for its Double Nep denim it uses nep yarn in both the warp and the weft rather than the usual one. Neps are the small knots and flecks of short cotton fiber that show up as pale specks and bumps on the surface, and doubling them gives this 16oz selvedge denim a dry, rough, uneven hand closer to homespun cloth than to conventional denim. The DNP-019-IDSM puts that fabric on the brand's relaxed tapered cut.

Color does the rest. The warp is rope-dyed indigo; the weft is dyed with sumi, the ink of Japanese calligraphy, made from natural soot bound with glue and ground with water before it is applied to the yarn. product.body_html:
Paper in the weft. Washi is the handmade Japanese paper drawn from the inner bark of mulberry and mitsumata, thin, fibrous, faintly translucent and far stronger than it looks; it has been made for more than a thousand years for calligraphy, shoji screens, bookbinding and art. Samurai Jeans spins that paper into yarn and weaves it into the weft of a 15oz selvedge denim, against a warp of extra-long staple Texas cotton with a soft, almost silky hand. The blend comes out at 60% cotton, 40% washi.

The effect is unusual for its weight. The washi weft makes the fabric lighter, cooler and more breathable than a conventional 15oz denim while keeping the texture and structure Samurai is known for, so the cloth sits at the heavy end of midweight without feeling like it. The yarn is hand dyed with natural indigo harvested from the Tokushima prefecture in Japan. Only a handful of indigo craftsmen are capable of this dyeing technique. It is certified by the Japanese government as a national living treasure.

The lengthy fermenting process required to produce natural indigo and the low annual output make this a highly coveted dye material. The undyed cotton yarns are dipped by hand into indigo dye vats repeatedly until the indigo has penetrated the core of the yarns.

For this reason, natural indigo jeans have a reputation for retaining their color. Most jeans use indigo dyed yarns that are white at the core, since they have not fully absorbed the indigo. The top layer of indigo will eventually give way to the white centers with moderate wear and abrasion. Natural indigo models hold their blue color longer making them tougher to break in, but this adds to their uniqueness.

We love a cardigan and we think 3sixteen nails them every season. These simple v-neck cardigans are constructed from a Suri alpaca/wool blend for a lightweight, warm and textured piece of knitwear. The rare Suri alpaca is known to be extremely soft and having a slightly hairy look to the yarn.

  • 74% Suri Alpaca 22% Wool 4% Polyamide

  • Knit in Peru
  • Dry clean

product.body_html:

product.title: 3sixteen Tanker Jacker - Black Twill
product.body_html:

Constructed from a substantial black twill outer and the interior is flannel lined for maximum comfort The jacket is insulated with Thermore filling, an eco-friendly synthetic down alternative, known for it's heat retention. 

  • 100% Cotton
  • Thermore fill

product.title: Brain Dead Type 00 15.5oz Slub Denim - Indigo
product.body_html:

The denim has a wonderful slub and feels heavier than 15.5oz but we feel these are going to break in real nice. Super cool accents including the batwing back pocket stitch design, scalloped front pockets w/ bat wing accent and rivets at high stress points.

  • Unsanforized. Wash in cold water + hang dry to minimize shrinkage.
  • Cut and sewn in Los Angeles

product.title: Iron Heart IH-1955S-142 14oz Selvedge Denim "1955" Vintage Tapered Cut Jeans - Indigo
product.body_html:
Iron Heart's newest cut of jean. The 1955 is based on a Levis 501 from 1955, which is a higher rise jean with a taper from the knee down resulting in a vintage style, relaxed fit. This iteration is in their "least heavy" 14oz denim, which is lighter in feel compared to their 21oz option but still packs a punch. This denim is made with a double twisted weft yarn, the same construction technique as their 21oz selvedge denim.

  • Made in Japan 
  • Vintage tapered cut
  • High rise
  • 14oz Japanese selvedge denim
  • Woven with a double twisted weft yarn (the same as our 21oz Selvedge denim)
  • Lined rear pockets
  • Button fly and hidden rivets
  • Belt loops sewn into waistband
  • Poly/cotton constructional stitching
  • Selvedge side seams and fly construction
  • Sanforized and one-washed - little to no shrinkage to be expected.
  • The waist will stretch out approximately one inch with wear
  • Other dimensions will stretch proportionately to the waist
